newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds surge, boosted by Letes auction.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds surge, boosted by Letes auction.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished sharply higher Tuesday, boosted by a well-received monthly Letes Treasury bill auction.
"There is an impressive boom in the market," said the chief bond trader at an Argentine bank.
The surge was led by peso-denominated bonds as the bills auction showed another reduction in the premium of peso instruments.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 3/4 to 91-3/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.32 to 126.25.
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 rose 0.68 pesos to 104.50.

The Economy Ministry placed 250 million pesos of 91-day treasury bills at a discount strike rate of 6.10 percent and $250 million of 182-day bills at 6.09 percent. The rates were much lower than expected.

Traders said the demand at the auction showed once again the very high domestic and international liquidity levels that have boosted the market recently. The auction showed those liquidity levels remain high, promising to feed more demand for bonds.
Call money rates fell to 5.88 percent from 5.90 percent.
